Π: the sum over all i ≠ a equals the sum over the strictly positive turns because every i ≠ a has τ_i ≥ 0 and zero terms contribute nothing (elementary; recorded as helper `sum_pos_turns_eq_sum_erase`, stmt 215-218, not under review). So the first conjunct is Π − α = 2π r with r = rot(L), the second is r ≥ 1. No printed clause is missing; no Lean clause is unprinted apart from `[NeZero c]`.

DOMAIN. ROT. `CV.rot L hL = rotRay L r = Σ_i epsRot L r i` at a chosen admissible r (Rotation.lean:113-118); `epsRot` (58-62) is the printed ε_i case split with the three determinants in the same order and the same signs (`det u v = u.1*v.2 − u.2*v.1`, Polygon.lean:16), and `Admissible` (66) is "det(r,δ_i) ≠ 0 for all i"; `rotRay_indep`/`rot_eq_rotRay` (365-372) give independence of r. CLAUSE (i) (stmt 274-285). `∀ i, 0 < principalTurn L i` is the strict "positive" (the printed proof says "each τ_i > 0", excerpt 17-18); `1 ≤ rot L hL` is rot ≥ 1; `c = 3` is "L has three corners" (def:rot names the corners q_0..q_{c−1}, so c is the corner count); `rot L hL = 1` is the equality. `∀ i, principalTurn L i < 0 → rot L hL ≤ −1` is the negative claim. `neg_three : … → c = 3 → rot L hL = −1` versus printed |rot(L)| = 1: these are equivalent inside the bundle because `neg_le_neg_one` (280-281) holds for the same c, L, hL under the same hypothesis, and rot ≤ −1 ∧ |rot| = 1 ⟺ rot ≤ −1 ∧ rot = −1.
